presented_options.A: ARIES-style WAL with explicit undo and redo records plus a separate dirty-page table checkpoint
presented_options.B: synchronous double-write: every page is written to a scratch region before being written to its home location

presented_options.D: shadow paging: mutations go to a copy page; a pointer swap at commit promotes the copy atomically

answers.rationale: Append-only WAL; on startup the recovery routine replays WAL up to the last COMMIT record and discards the uncommitted suffix.

presented_options.A: records are padded to a fixed 512-byte sector boundary; partial sectors are discarded
presented_options.B: no per-record check; a single CRC covers the whole WAL file on clean shutdown

answers.rationale: Each WAL record embeds a CRC32 (using crc32fast); replay verifies each record's CRC and stops at the first mismatch.

presented_options.C: vectorised/columnar execution where each operator produces and consumes batches of column vectors
presented_options.D: a Volcano-style iterator tree: each operator exposes open/next/close and returns one row (or tiny batch) at a time

answers.rationale: Physical operators implement a Volcano-style open/next/close trait returning one row at a time.

presented_options.A: all three rows — every fsynced WAL record is replayed on startup
presented_options.B: the two earliest rows — only WAL records that survive the CRC check are replayed; the trailing one is dropped
presented_options.C: no rows — a transaction whose WAL trail has no COMMIT record is treated as an uncommitted prefix and discarded
presented_options.D: an error at startup demanding manual recovery before any SELECT can run

answers.rationale: Recovery only replays WAL records up to the last COMMIT; a transaction with no COMMIT record is treated as uncommitted and discarded.
